artboards.title: Option A — the This cycle strip
Option B — Progress back in the tab bar
Option C — Progress becomes a tab of You

annotations.text:
THE FINDING

app.jsx:17967 records why Progress left the tab bar, and why that was safe: "nothing daily is lost, because the verdict, the weight spark and the weekly check-in prompt all live on the StatusCard there."

StatusCard no longer exists — that comment is its last mention in the file. The demotion was paid for with a Today presence that was later deleted, and nobody restored it.

This frame is the consequence: nothing on Today answers whether the plan is working.

OPTION A — CHOSEN

Restore the compensation, not the tab. One strip between the buddy and the plan: verdict, trend weight, the 90-day shape, one tap into the full page.

94px at rest, and the plan card still clears the fold (~683px of 693px usable). It grows only when the check-in is due or the read is thin — the rule BuddyHabitat already follows.

Still open: this makes Progress VISIBLE, not a destination. The settings-overview card stays its only front door until something like Option C lands.

OPTION B — not taken

Progress back in the tab bar. Drawn at the shipped component's real geometry: BottomNav's FAB is a flex-1 sibling, so a fifth tab makes six equal children share 374px — ~62px each, and PROGRESS at 9px Silkscreen tracked 0.08em does not fit its cell.

The frequency argument that moved it out also still stands: a weekly read holding a daily slot, and Today still saying nothing about progress.

OPTION C — not taken (yet)

The strip You already has grows to Progress | Settings | Account, lands on Progress, and the settings-overview card that carries it today goes.

This is the half that actually answers "hidden in settings" — Option A makes Progress visible on Today, but reaching the full page still means going through a settings list.

Tradeoff: the header button still says YOU behind a gear, which then under-promises what is behind it.
